newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean stocks rally to the close on CERJ deal.
newsitem.headline: Chilean stocks rally to the close on CERJ deal.

text.p: Chilean stocks rallied to the close in heavy trade powered by electrical shares on a Chilean-led consortium's purchase of Brazilian utility CERJ, brokers said.

A string of bullish news development on various fronts pushed the blue-chip IPSA index up 1.33 percent to 95.83 points at the close. The all-share IGPA index ended up one percent to 5228.59 points, snapping a series of declines.
"There has been a lot of good news, and I think the bolsa might have broken its losing trend," said one broker.

What had looked like a merely technical rise early in the session gathered force as news hit the market that a consortium led by Enersis and its distribution unit Chilectra had won 60 percent of Rio de Janeiro's CERJ in a privatization tender.
The rise dragged up electrical stocks in general and particularly those related to holding company Enersis.
Enersis ended 2.1 percent higher at 246 pesos, while Chilectra was one of the day's top gainers, ending 3.8 percent higher at 295 pesos. Endesa ended 1.2 percent higher to 246 pesos.
An agreement in Congress on the 1997 budget also added to the bolsa's buoyant sentiment, after Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat and the opposition wrapped up negotiations, brokers said.
Higher copper prices and expectations for low November inflation also added to the bullish momentum, brokers said.

There are only two copper mining companies quoted on the bourse, but higher copper prices tend to ease pressure on inflation and interest rates. About 40 percent of Chile's export income comes from the red metal.
Other gainers included Laboratorio Chile, up 3.7 percent to 360 pesos, and Copec, up 1.6 percent to 1625 pesos, snapping a recent slide.
Andina ended 0.5 percent higher at 2140 pesos after company officials said they expected stronger sales in their Brazilian operations next year after a slack 1996.
There were only a handful of decliners in the final trading session. Inforsa ended down 2.7 percent to close at 73 pesos and Cruz Blanca slipped three percent to 159 pesos.
